chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated from Abu Saeed al-Adami, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umair, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir, who said: We heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

"This matter (the rise of the Mahdi) will not take place until two-thirds of the people perish." We asked: "If two-thirds of the people perish, who will remain?" He replied: "Are you not satisfied that you will be among the remaining one-third?"

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: The matter/authority (referring to the Imam or the Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the remaining one-third of people in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the 'test' (ibtila') of the Shia during the Great Occultation is framed through the lens of divine selection, where the survival of the faithful is linked to the purification of the world. The Imam’s rhetorical question, 'Are you not pleased to be in the remaining third?', transforms the demographic reduction from a mere tragedy into a mark of honor, emphasizing that endurance through tribulation ensures one's place among the elect. This concept aligns with the Shia understanding of the occultation as a period of spiritual refinement rather than abandonment.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 286 - Muhammad bin Ja’far Asadi has narrated from Abu Saeed Adami from Muhammad bin Husain for Muhammad bin Abi Umair Abi Ayyub from Muhammad bin Muslim and Abu Basir that he said: We heard Abi Abdullah (a.s) say:

“It will not take place till two-third of the human population does not perish.” He was asked: “If two-third perishes, who will remain?” He replied: “Are you not satisfied that one-third will remain?”
